shortDescription: Conduits attack hostile mobs at every active tier, within half the Conduit Power radius
oneLiner: Your conduit shoots hostile mobs as soon as it is active (16 frame blocks) instead of only at the full 42-block frame, and it reaches out to half its Conduit Power radius instead of a flat 8 blocks.
mixins: conduit_attack_range.ConduitBlockEntityMixin (listed under "mixins" = both sides, vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json:16, and as the standalone jar's only mixin, build.gradle:411-412; targets net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.ConduitBlockEntity with 4 injections: 1x @ModifyConstant(intValue = 42) on updateDestroyTarget, 2x @Redirect on updateDestroyTarget (getDestroyRangeAABB -> frame-scaled box, BlockPos.closerThan -> same scaled radius) and 1x @Redirect on findDestroyTarget (getDestroyRangeAABB -> maxHostileRadius box, for the client attack beam))

configKeys.effect: Hostile-damage radius = Conduit Power radius (frames / 7 * 16) / this divisor, floored at 1 block. 2 (default) = half the effect radius: 16 blocks at 16 frames, 48 at 42. 1 = full effect radius (32 / 96). The module additionally clamps the value with Math.max(1, ...).

Minimum frame-block count at which a conduit starts attacking hostiles, replacing vanilla's hardcoded 42. Values below 16 do nothing (vanilla only runs the attack tick on an ACTIVE conduit, which needs 16 frames) and values above 42 switch attacking off entirely (a vanilla frame caps at 42). Note the conduit's angry open-eye texture still needs 42 frames - the mixin does not touch updateHunting.

notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT (whole module, 3 files, nothing else): modules/conduit_attack_range/ConduitAttackRangeModule.java (88 lines), modules/conduit_attack_range/config/ConduitAttackRangeConfig.java, mixin/conduit_attack_range/ConduitBlockEntityMixin.java. Verified by find over both package trees plus a grep for DeferredRegister / @SubscribeEvent / EVENT_BUS / ModList / Dist. / Minecraft.getInstance / KeyMapping / registerCommand / shouldInitialize / isEnabledByDefault across them: zero hits. So: no registries, no events, no commands, no keybinds, no compat package, no JEI plugin, no recipes, no loot hooks, no shouldInitialize gate, no isEnabledByDefault override (Module.java:73 default true applies). No lang keys either: grepping "conduit" in en_us.json only hits block.vanillaplusadditions.end_conduit, which belongs to the unrelated end_conduit module. No TODO/FIXME/HACK markers, no dead code (isActive, minFrames, hostileRadius, maxHostileRadius are all called from the mixin or from each other).

NO EVENT SUBSCRIPTIONS AT ALL. onInitialize() only writes one info log line ("Conduit Attack Range module initialized - conduits now hunt at every tier"). All behaviour lives in the mixin, which is ALWAYS applied (listed unconditionally in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json) and self-gates at runtime via ConduitAttackRangeModule.isActive().

BIGGEST FINDING - THE STANDALONE JAR IS A DUD. build.gradle:411-412 declares moduleId conduit_attack_range / modId vpa_conduit_attack_range / displayName 'Vanilla Plus: Conduit Attack Range' with only the one mixin (no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps), and moduleJar_conduit_attack_range therefore builds and CI publishes it (release.yml:49 `./gradlew moduleJars`, release.yml:88 attaches build/libs/modules/*.jar). BUT the jar task packs `standalone/${entrypointPkg}/**` (build.gradle:642) and there is NO src/main/java/.../standalone/conduit_attack_range/ package - it has never existed in git history. Of all 40 standaloneModules entries only conduit_attack_range and end_conduit lack their @Mod entrypoint; every other module has one (pattern: standalone/<id>/<Name>Standalone.java calling StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot(new <Name>Module(), ...)). Consequence, provable from the code: without that entrypoint the module object is never constructed, so the static `instance` stays null, isActive() returns false and the mixin returns vanilla values - the standalone jar ships literally no behaviour. (Whether NeoForge additionally refuses to load a javafml mod file with no @Mod class cannot be decided from this repo.) hasStandaloneJar is kept true because the descriptor and the jar exist, but it is not usable.

RADIUS MATH (ConduitAttackRangeModule.hostileRadius): effectRadius = frameCount / 7 * 16 (integer division), then / max(1, radius_divisor), then Math.max(1, ...). That mirror of vanilla's Conduit Power radius is exact - the compiled 1.21.1 ConduitBlockEntity.applyEffects computes `size / 7 * 16` the same way. With the default divisor 2: 16 frames -> 16 blocks, 21 -> 24, 42 -> 48. Frame counts below 7 would yield effectRadius 0 and are clamped to 1, but cannot occur in practice (see the min_frames note). The divisor is clamped with Math.max(1, ...) in the module on top of the config range, so a corrupt 0 cannot divide by zero.

FALLBACKS: the module's static helpers return hardcoded vanilla-ish defaults when `instance` is null (minFrames -> 16, hostileRadius -> divisor 2; maxHostileRadius just delegates), and the config getters return 2 / 16 while the ModConfigSpec values are not built yet. The documented defaults therefore hold even pre-config.

GOTCHA - min_frames' configurable range is far wider than what does anything. The config allows 1..96, but the EFFECTIVE range is 16..42: vanilla only calls updateDestroyTarget for an ACTIVE conduit (serverTick bytecode: `if (updateShape(...)) { applyEffects(...); updateDestroyTarget(...); }`, and updateShape returns size >= 16), so any value below 16 changes nothing; and a vanilla frame caps at 42 blocks (MAX_FRAMES), so any value above 42 silently means "this conduit never attacks". Nothing validates or warns.

GOTCHA - the angry eye still needs 42 frames. Vanilla's updateHunting sets the isHunting flag from `positions.size() >= 42` and the mixin does not touch it (@ModifyConstant is scoped to method = "updateDestroyTarget"). ConduitRenderer picks OPEN_EYE_TEXTURE only when isHunting() is true. So with the default min_frames = 16 a sub-42 conduit attacks and damages mobs while its eye stays closed - a purely cosmetic mismatch, but it is what a player sees.

GOTCHA - the disabled path does NOT call the original method. Both AABB redirects (vpaDestroyRange, vpaFindDestroyRange) rebuild the box themselves as new AABB(x,y,z,x+1,y+1,z+1).inflate(8) when the module is off instead of delegating to ConduitBlockEntity.getDestroyRangeAABB. That is byte-for-byte what vanilla 1.21.1's helper does today (verified in its bytecode: block box, then .inflate(8.0)), so it is currently equivalent - but a Minecraft change there would be silently reimplemented wrong.

GOTCHA - the injection points are broad by construction. @ModifyConstant(constant = @Constant(intValue = 42)) hits EVERY literal 42 inside updateDestroyTarget and the @Redirect on BlockPos.closerThan(Vec3i, D) hits EVERY such call in that method. In 1.21.1 there is exactly one of each (see VANILLA VERIFICATION), so the mixin is precise today; a Minecraft update adding a second would be captured too, unnoticed.

VANILLA VERIFICATION (evidence from OUTSIDE the repo - the Gradle-cached, renamed 1.21.1 ConduitBlockEntity/ConduitRenderer class files under ~/.gradle/caches/ng_execute, javap-ed; the repo itself checks in no Minecraft sources): updateDestroyTarget contains exactly one `bipush 42`, exactly one call to getDestroyRangeAABB and exactly one BlockPos.closerThan(Vec3i,D) (with the constant 8.0) - so all three injectors bind 1:1 under injectors.defaultRequire = 1. findDestroyTarget contains exactly one getDestroyRangeAABB call. serverTick calls updateDestroyTarget every 40 game ticks and the damage is hurt(damageSources().magic(), 4.0F) - confirming the module javadoc's "4 magic damage every 2 seconds", which the mixin leaves untouched.

SIDE: "both", and it is genuinely both. The mixin sits in the shared "mixins" block of vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json (line 16), not in "client". updateDestroyTarget is reached only from ConduitBlockEntity.serverTick (server: target pick, retain check, damage), while findDestroyTarget is reached from clientTick -> updateClientTarget (client: resolve the target by UUID so the attack beam/particles render) AND from updateDestroyTarget itself on the server after a reload. The module contains no rendering, keybinds, Dist.CLIENT or Minecraft.getInstance() references.

LIVE TOGGLING: isActive() -> isModuleEnabled() -> ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled(moduleId, config.isEnabled()), which consults the runtime override map first (setRuntimeModuleEnabled) and otherwise the live config value, and the mixin re-reads config on every call. So `enabled`, radius_divisor and min_frames all take effect immediately - no world reload, no restart. Framework detail worth knowing: in the bundle, onInitialize() runs for EVERY registered module regardless of the config, because ModuleManager.initializeModules (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:117) runs before the config spec is even built (registerConfig at :131), so the enabled probe falls back to the default; the "module initialized" log line therefore appears even when the module is switched off in the toml. The real gate is the per-call isModuleEnabled() check.

DOC STATUS: there is NO docs/modules/conduit_attack_range.md. README.md lines 95-96 are the only prose ("attack hostile mobs at every active tier (not just at full size), within half the Conduit Power radius, and fixes the client-side attack beam"). That is accurate but glosses over two things: "within half the Conduit Power radius" is only the default (radius_divisor) and "every active tier" is only the default (min_frames = 16); both are configurable. It also does not mention the closed-eye mismatch.

HISTORY: module + mixin + bundle registration + mixins.json entry + the build.gradle standalone descriptor all landed together in 80f146b (2026-07-21), first tag v1.0.0-beta.43. The 4th injection (@Redirect on findDestroyTarget widening the search box to maxHostileRadius()) was NOT in that commit; it came in 8051624 (2026-07-22, "fix(cat_guardian, conduit_attack_range): base-metal armor repair + client attack beam"), first tag v1.0.0-beta.45. So: module since v1.0.0-beta.43, working attack beam beyond 8 blocks since v1.0.0-beta.45. maxHostileRadius() is evaluated at the CURRENT divisor for 42 frames (48 blocks by default, 96 with radius_divisor = 1), and that box is inflated on every findDestroyTarget call on both sides; the author notes it is safe because the lookup matches an exact UUID.
